standard_prerequisites.name: An affine morphism is separated, and the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module along it is a quasi-coherent module on the base, cited by the author from the same chapter and from the schemes chapter

standard_prerequisites.name: Adjunction between pullback and pushforward, and the algebra structure on the pullback of the pushforward algebra together with its map to the structure sheaf
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 1928-1937 to define the quasi-inverse and at 1938-1945 to build the two comparison maps
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the quasi-inverse as a tensor product over the pulled-back algebra and the unit and counit transformations.

standard_prerequisites.name: The same-chapter statement that a module over a quasi-coherent algebra is quasi-coherent over the base if and only if it is quasi-coherent over the algebra
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: This is the author's first sentence, at proof line 1921, disposing of the final assertion by citation
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the author's own disposition of the moreover part of the statement; the counted proof itself constructs the equivalence of categories.

core_obligations: Establish the functor: for an affine, hence separated, morphism the pushforward of a quasi-coherent module is quasi-coherent on the base by the two cited statements, so the pushforward is a functor between the two categories in the statement (proof lines 1922-1926).

Construct a quasi-inverse h by sending a quasi-coherent module over the pushforward algebra A to the tensor product of its pullback with the structure sheaf over the pulled-back algebra, and note that this is again quasi-coherent because quasi-coherence is preserved by pullback and by change of rings (proof lines 1928-1937).

Build the two comparison maps: the counit from h applied to a pushforward to the original module, coming from the adjunction map, and the unit from a module to the pushforward of h applied to it, adjoint to the map sending a local section to its tensor product with one (proof lines 1938-1945).

Finish by reducing to the affine case, where the verification of the two comparison maps is the algebra identity that the tensor product of a module with the tensor product algebra, tensored down to the algebra again, returns the module; the author states this identity as the key observation making the argument work (proof lines 1947-1965).
proof_roadmap: Get the functor from quasi-coherence of pushforwards along an affine morphism (proof lines 1922-1926), then build an explicit quasi-inverse by base change of modules over the pushforward algebra (proof lines 1928-1937).
Compare the two composites through the unit and counit of the adjunction and verify them on an affine covering, where the proof reduces to a single algebra identity (proof lines 1938-1965).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the module version of the affine equivalence: for an affine morphism f with pushforward algebra A, the pushforward gives an equivalence from quasi-coherent modules on X to quasi-coherent modules over A, and a module over A is quasi-coherent over the base exactly when it is quasi-coherent over A (statement lines 1895-1919). The counted proof constructs the quasi-inverse explicitly as a tensor product over the pulled-back algebra, then produces the unit and counit of the adjunction and reduces their verification to a single algebra identity (proof lines 1922-1965). It is H2: the construction is carried out in full and the argument is not a citation, but the last sentence of the statement is disposed of by the author with a citation to a same-chapter lemma, and the verification of the algebra identity is left to the reader with the author's phrase 'We omit the details'; the counted content is therefore the explicit construction of the equivalence and of its comparison maps.
